summary: Sapna Goyal (Mayo College), Mishi Sardana (Southampton), and Iqra Khan (Durham) walked counselors through the two structural changes to the UK's UCAS application for the new cycle: the personal statement moved from a single 4,000-character box to three structured prompts (each requiring at least 350 characters), and the Letter of Reference (LOR) was split into three sections -- School Context, Extenuating Circumstances, and Academic Suitability. Panelists repeatedly warned that admissions officers will not click external links (GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolios) included in a personal statement, and walked through live case reviews and audience polling on what belongs in each LOR section.
keyInsights: UCAS personal statement: 3 structured prompts, minimum 350 characters each, total cap remains 4,000 characters.
UCAS LOR is now split into 3 sections: School Context, Extenuating Circumstances, and Academic Suitability.
Hard rule repeated by multiple panelists: admissions officers do not click external links (GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio, YouTube).
